# Competitive Platform Analysis

Curated by Skill Harbor: a competitive landscape scoping skill that decides who to benchmark and where to find them before any scoring begins. The premise: a competitive analysis is only as good as its frame; the wrong set makes the client look either unbeatable or doomed. Step one is non-negotiable: establish the client's positioning brief (identity and aesthetic register, offer, target clients, differentiator, scoping consequence, strategic tension) through a short interview, never invented, never scoped blind. Then populate eight generic axes so the landscape is not skewed toward one archetype: positioning stance (brand-led versus capability-led), specialization (specialist versus generalist), size and model (solo to enterprise), engagement format (productized versus bespoke), distinctiveness posture (conventional versus contrarian), evidence model (outcome-led versus aesthetic-led), brand strength of the operator, and market reach. Candidates resolve into three tiers: Direct (same band, overlapping offer, same targets), Adjacent (partial overlap pressing at the edges), Aspirational (the bar to aim at), plus substitutes noted as a threat vector. A lightweight 1-to-5 pre-filter scoring matrix decides who graduates to full benchmarking, with rules of thumb per the client's scoping consequence (high distinctiveness plus high credibility means must-profile; memorable but un-hireable is a cautionary case). Data sources are matched to dimensions: portfolios, awards, the...
